unresolvedReferences.description: All Western years in this chunk convert Shaoxing (紹興) years with external Song reign chronology (Shaoxing 1 = AD 1131); the packet has no Song reign mapping. The packet English already gives the same years. Jingkang (from 1126) and Jianyan (1127–1130) era dates used for bounds are also external.
上/帝/陛下 in s0035–s0047 are identified as Emperor Gaozong of Song by external knowledge (the reigning emperor in the Shaoxing era); the chapter does not name him.
The 'five men' promoted with Xiang Sisheng are taken to be Sisheng and the four Peng leaders named in s0027 (strongly inferred).
歸明 is read as the status 'submitted', qualifying three prefectures (Baojing, Nanwei, Yongshun); a repair is proposed.

帝 in s0058, s0070 and s0077 is identified as Emperor Xiaozong of Song by external knowledge (the reigning emperor in the Longxing and Qiandao eras); the chapter does not name him.
當年 is read as the given name of Li Angxiao's son (with the packet English); the surname Li is inferred. Likewise Tian Zhongzuo's surname (s0071) is inferred from his father.
明椿 is read as the personal name of the commander stationed at Jing and E (荊、鄂駐紮); his full title is not given.
Zhao Shangu's memorial is not dated; it is placed after the Qiandao 6 (AD 1170) entry, so only an on-or-after bound is given.

Western years in this chunk convert Qiandao (乾道) years with external Song reign chronology (Qiandao 7 = AD 1171, Qiandao 8 = AD 1172); the packet has no Song reign mapping. The packet English already gives the same years. Jingkang (from AD 1126), Chongning and Jianyan era dates are also external.
帝 in s0105 and s0110 is identified as Emperor Xiaozong of Song by external knowledge; the chapter does not name him.

The reign dates of Shenzong (AD 1067–1085) and Huizong (AD 1100–1126) are external and not stated in the chapter. 桂府 is identified as the Gui Prefecture seat (modern Guilin) by external knowledge; a repair is proposed.
s0081–s0082 continue Zhao Shangu's memorial from chunk 002a; he is not named in this chunk, so no person record is repeated here.

The dating of Tian Shiluo and Gong Zhineng's occupation is only bounded: after the Jingkang troubles (external start AD 1126) and before Zhang Caishao's memorial of Qiandao 7 (AD 1171, external conversion).

十年 (s0111) and 十一年 (s0123) have no era name. The packet English converts them as Qiandao 10–11 (AD 1174–1175), but by external chronology Qiandao had only nine years (AD 1165–1173). They are taken as Chunxi 10–11 (AD 1183–1184) by external inference, which is uncertain; repairs are proposed. External recollection also supports the later date: Chen Dong's Guiyang revolt, cited as past in s0116, is dated c. AD 1179.
Jiatai 3 = AD 1203, Jiading 1/2/5/7 = AD 1208/1209/1212/1214, Kaibao 8 = AD 975, and Taiping Xingguo 2 = AD 977 are external conversions; the packet has no Song reign mapping.
帝 in s0135 and s0139 is identified as Emperor Ningzong of Song by external knowledge (the reigning emperor in the Jiatai era); the chapter does not name him.

The Wugang rebel Yang Zaixing (s0116) may be the Wugang chief Yang Zaixing of chunk 001 (father of Yang Zhengxiu); this is not asserted. He is not the famous general Yang Zaixing (external knowledge).
世祿 in s0127 is taken as a textual variant of 友祿 (Yang Youlu, s0125); the packet idiomatic already reads 'Youlu'.
押隊 is read as a military rank (external knowledge), so the person is Hou, a squad leader; a repair is proposed.
Li Jin and Yao Mingjiao, cited in s0154, match rebels dated in chunk 002a (Qiandao 1 and 3); cross-chunk identity is left to the merge.

上 (s0217) and 朕 (s0219, s0222) are identified as Emperor Taizong of Song by external knowledge (the reigning emperor in the Yongxi era); the chapter does not name him.

昌運 is read as a person heading a group of five appointees, parallel to 晟情等十六人; a repair is proposed. The surnames of Changyun, Shengqing, Guangjian, Riyan, Changda and Tongying are inferred as Yang from the clan context and are not stated.
This Yang Shengtai (active AD 1087–1102 by derived bounds) shares a name with a rebel cited as 'recent' in the Jiading 5 (AD 1212) memorial in chunk 003; identity is not asserted.
縣民莫世家牛 may name a county resident Mo Shijia; with the packet English it is read as 'the Mo household', and no person record is made.
Yang Chang (楊昌), listed with Changda as Guangjian's son(s), may be a truncated name; his sonship is strongly inferred from the construction 光僭之子……昌達、……楊昌等.
